title: Localization of the normalized inverse scalar square
statement: Let l,E,L,g,hX,hY be as in [def-pod-isomorphism-field-transport-clauses], let iota:E→L be a Q_l-algebra homomorphism, and let SE and SL be normalized single-field transport packages at E and L. Assume isomorphismFieldTransportScalarLaw(l,E,L,iota,g), the integral inverse/scalar equation. Then isomorphismFieldTransportRationalScalarLaw(l,E,L,iota,g,hX,hY,SE,SL) holds on every raw rational object. This only localizes the one given equation and does not construct transport packages or descend a family to Ω.

proof.text: Write each rational object as the localization of its underlying integral object. The stage formulas identify its rational epsilon with localization of integral epsilon. The specified rational scalar comparison identifies alpha with localization of the integral scalar comparison.

proof.text: Apply the integral-to-rational functor to the assumed scalar equation. The pure-tensor pullback formula at coefficient one, and the semilinear scalar-extension formula at coefficient one, identify each resulting factor with the stated rational factors. Use functorial preservation of composition. The object equalities provide the HEq endpoint transports; the result is the displayed equality on each rational object. Naturality is that of the existing rational transformations, so it covers all localized arrows.
